title: Outlook: custom organisation properties on profile cards
summary: Hold: the connector gallery route starts inside the gallery rather than telling administrators how to reach it. The rollout, opt-in default and data-exposure warnings are supported; the licensing field and the formatting of both Graph calls need smaller corrections.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans custom organisation-specific profile card properties sourced from external systems such as HR platforms.
claims.quote: These properties can be sourced from external systems like HR platforms, enriching user profiles with relevant organizational details.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model, licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because no licence requirement specific to this new feature is published.
claims.quote: Your tenant must have Microsoft 365 licenses. The surfaces available to your users ... and the connector types you can deploy depend on your organization's licensing.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included and state: 'The connector prerequisites require Microsoft 365 licenses for the tenant; available connector types and surfaces depend on licensing. A licence requirement specific to these new custom profile card properties is not yet published.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/prerequisites. Keep cost low and the narrower feature-specific licensing gap.

claims.claim: No API for configuring the new connector-sourced custom-property visibility, display name and icon is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: profile cards connector custom properties visibility display name icon Graph API person info profile cards; "profile" "connector" "custom" "icon" API visibility. Read add-properties-profilecard, Create profileCardProperty, externalConnection and the build guide; no such call stated.

claims.claim: Connectors gallery > Human resources & recruiting is the admin-center navigation route for choosing a people-data connector.
claims.quote: In the left pane, choose Copilot > Connectors. On the Connectors tab, in the left pane, choose Gallery, and select the data source you want to connect
claims.fix: Replace controls[1].ui.path and its rendered route with 'Copilot > Connectors > Gallery > Human resources & recruiting'. Keep the peopleconnectors docs link for the category and add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/connectors/deployment-overview to sources for the navigation. Replace 'Learn gives the gallery, not a click path' with 'Choose the people-data source in the Human resources & recruiting category.'

claims.where: controls[1].api; Governance controls: table and notes
claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections creates a people-data connection when contentCategory is people.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections
claims.fix: Set controls[1].api.call and the rendered call to 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/external/connections'. In the note say: 'The request body sets the top-level contentCategory property to people.' The v1.0 externalConnection resource documents that property at https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/externalconnectors-externalconnection.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Governance controls: table and notes
claims.claim: Existing optional profile-card properties are configured at Settings > Org settings > People settings > Profile card > Contact info.
claims.quote: admins can configure their visibility by navigating to Settings > Org settings > People settings > Profile card > Contact info in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.fix: Expand controls[2].ui.path and its rendered route to 'Settings > Org settings > Services > People settings > Profile card > Contact info'. The already-cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/admin/manage/people-settings-in-microsoft-365-admin-center gives the Services tab that lists People settings.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/people/profileCardProperties configures Entra profile-card properties using directoryPropertyName, annotations and isVisible.
claims.quote: Use the annotations and directoryPropertyName properties on profileCardProperty to configure profile card properties. You can also use the isVisible property to indicate whether the given directory property should be shown on a user's profile card.
claims.fix: Set controls[2].api.call and the rendered call to 'POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/admin/people/profileCardProperties'. Add to the note: 'The request body specifies directoryPropertyName, annotations for labels, and isVisible for visibility.' Remove the parenthesised property list from the call.

claims.claim: The existing profile card API covers Microsoft Entra attributes, including CustomAttribute1 through CustomAttribute15.
claims.quote: You can add any of the 15 Microsoft Entra ID custom extension attributes to users' profile cards

claims.claim: Microsoft has not confirmed that the existing Entra profile-card property API governs the new connector-sourced custom properties.
claims.quote: Searched: profile cards connector custom properties visibility display name icon Graph API person info profile cards; opened add-properties-profilecard, Create profileCardProperty and read profileCardProperty search excerpts. The API specifies Entra directory properties, not connector custom properties.
